svg.title: MarkeTech backend: the data model
svg.desc: Entity-relationship diagram of the MarkeTech backend: twelve models in eight Django apps. accounts: User, identified by a unique e-mail address. profiles: CandidateProfile and EmployerProfile, each one-to-one with a User, and CandidateDocument under a candidate profile. offers: JobOffer under an employer profile. favorites: Favorite, unique per candidate and offer. applications: JobApplication, unique per offer and candidate, with its StatusChange history and its Attachment copies. messaging: Message on an application, written by a User. appointments: Appointment on an application, one pending at a time. reviews: Review, one per User, scores from 1 to 5. Every foreign key cascades on delete.
svg.text: The tables of the application's own models (backend/*/models.py), grouped by Django app, with their links and the rules the
database itself enforces. notifications, live and demo have no model. Real code of the repository at commit a7f8fb3 (30.10.2026).
How to read it: an arrow goes from the table holding the foreign key to the table it points to; 0..N and 1 say how many rows
on each side. Every foreign key is on_delete=CASCADE: deleting an account removes its profile, offers, applications and all that hangs on them.

svg.text: admin log) and the e-mail address tables that
allauth.account adds. The User's two many-to-many
AbstractUser. The models declare no ManyToMany
field of their own: Favorite is the link table
The values listed under a field (draft | published |
closed, ...) are checked by Django and the API, not
by the database: no CHECK constraint on them, except
of the TextFields are not in the database either.
A FILE field keeps only a relative path in the
database. The files are under MEDIA_ROOT, the Docker
volume media in production: candidates/<user id>/,
applications/<user id>/<offer id>/ for the copies
sent with an application. A view of the API checks
who may read a file before serving it.
foreign key, to the table it points to
